studies.title: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and its Sulphate (DHEAS) in Alzheimer's Disease.
studies.abstract: Neurosteroids Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulphate (DHEAS) are involved in many important brain functions, including neuronal plasticity and survival, cognition and behavior, demonstrating preventive and therapeutic potential in different neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease. The aim of the article was to provide a comprehensive overview of the literature on the involvement of DHEA and DHEAS in Alzheimer's disease. PubMed and MEDLINE databases were searched for relevant literature. The articles were selected considering their titles and abstracts. In the selected full texts, lists of references were searched manually for additional articles. We performed a systematic review of the studies investigating the role of DHEA and DHEAS in various in vitro and animal models, as well as in patients with Alzheimer's disease, and provided a comprehensive discussion on their potential preventive and therapeutic applications. Despite mixed results, the findings of various preclinical studies are generally supportive of the involvement of DHEA and DHEAS in the pathophysiology of Alzheimer's disease, showing some promise for potential benefits of these neurosteroids in the prevention and treatment. However, so far small clinical trials brought little evidence to support their therapy in AD. Therefore, large-scale human studies are needed to elucidate the specific effects of DHEA and DHEAS and their mechanisms of action, prior to their applications in clinical practice.

studies.title: Pregnenolone and dehydroepiandrosterone as an adjunctive treatment in schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder: an 8-week, double-blind, randomized, controlle
studies.abstract: Pregnenolone (PREG) and dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) are reported to have a modulatory effect on neuronal excitability, synaptic plasticity, and response to stress; they are associated with mood regulation and cognitive performance. We investigated the influence of PREG and DHEA on psychotic symptoms and cognitive functioning as an add-on to ongoing antipsychotic treatment of patients with chronic schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder. This 8-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, 2-center study compared 30 mg/d of PREG (PREG-30), 200 mg/d of PREG (PREG-200), 400 mg/d of DHEA, and placebo as an adjunctive treatment of 58 chronic schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder patients (DSM-IV). The data were collected from February 2005 until June 2007. The outcome measures were symptomatic and neurocognitive changes, functioning, and tolerability as assessed primarily by the Clinical Global Impressions-Severity of Illness scale and the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale. Analyses are presented for 44 patients who completed 8 weeks of treatment and for 14 noncompleters. Compared with subjects who received placebo, those administered PREG-30 had significant reductions in positive symptom scores and extrapyramidal side effects (EPS) and improvement in attention and working memory performance, whereas subjects treated with PREG-200 did not differ on outcome variable scores for the study period. The general psychopathology severity and general functioning of patients receiving placebo and PREG-30 improved more than that of those subjects treated with DHEA, while EPS improved more in subjects treated with DHEA than in patients receiving placebo. Negative symptoms and akathisia were not significantly benefited by any treatment. The administration of PREG and DHEA was well tolerated. Low-dose PREG augmentation demonstrated significant amelioration of positive symptoms and EPS and improvement in attention and working memory performance of schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder patients. Further double-blind controlled studies are needed to investigate the clinical benefit of pregnenolone augmentation. clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT00174889.

studies.title: Long-term DHEA replacement in primary adrenal insufficiency: a randomized, controlled trial.
studies.abstract: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and DHEA sulfate (DHEAS) are the major circulating adrenal steroids and substrates for peripheral sex hormone biosynthesis. In Addison's disease, glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid deficiencies require lifelong replacement, but the associated near-total failure of DHEA synthesis is not typically corrected. In a double-blind trial, we randomized 106 subjects (44 males, 62 females) with Addison's disease to receive either 50 mg daily of micronized DHEA or placebo orally for 12 months to evaluate its longer-term effects on bone mineral density, body composition, and cognitive function together with well-being and fatigue. Circulating DHEAS and androstenedione rose significantly in both sexes, with testosterone increasing to low normal levels only in females. DHEA reversed ongoing loss of bone mineral density at the femoral neck (P < 0.05) but not at other sites; DHEA enhanced total body (P = 0.02) and truncal (P = 0.017) lean mass significantly with no change in fat mass. At baseline, subscales of psychological well-being in questionnaires (Short Form-36, General Health Questionnaire-30), were significantly worse in Addison's patients vs. control populations (P < 0.001), and one subscale of SF-36 improved significantly (P = 0.004) after DHEA treatment. There was no significant benefit of DHEA treatment on fatigue or cognitive or sexual function. Supraphysiological DHEAS levels were achieved in some older females who experienced mild androgenic side effects. Although further long-term studies of DHEA therapy, with dosage adjustment, are desirable, our results support some beneficial effects of prolonged DHEA treatment in Addison's disease.

studies.title: Dhea supplementation and cognition in postmenopausal women.
studies.abstract: Previous work has suggested that DHEA supplementation may have adverse cognitive effects in elderly women. This article analyzed 24-h measurements of DHEA, DHEAS, and cortisol to determine if cognitive decrease with treatment is mediated by DHEA's impact on endogenous cortisol. It was found that DHEA administration increased cortisol at several hours during the day. In the treatment group, cortisol was positively associated with cognition at study completion. An increase in negative associations between DHEA(S) levels and cognition was found at completion. Increased cortisol does not explain the cognitive deficits associated with DHEA, suggesting a direct negative effect of exogenous DHEA on cognition.

studies.title: Effects of DHEA administration on episodic memory, cortisol and mood in healthy young men: a double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
studies.abstract: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) has been reported to enhance cognition in rodents, although there are inconsistent findings in humans. The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of DHEA administration in healthy young men on episodic memory and its neural correlates utilising an event-related potential (ERP) technique. Twenty-four healthy young men were treated with a 7-day course of oral DHEA (150 mg b.d.) or placebo in a double blind, random, crossover and balanced order design. Subjective mood and memory were measured using visual analogue scales (VASs). Cortisol concentrations were measured in saliva samples. ERPs were recorded during retrieval in an episodic memory test. Low-resolution brain electromagnetic tomography (LORETA) was used to identify brain regions involved in the cognitive task. DHEA administration led to a reduction in evening cortisol concentrations and improved VAS mood and memory. Recollection accuracy in the episodic memory test was significantly improved following DHEA administration. LORETA revealed significant hippocampal activation associated with successful episodic memory retrieval following placebo. DHEA modified ERPs associated with retrieval and led to a trend towards an early differential activation of the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). DHEA treatment improved memory recollection and mood and decreased trough cortisol levels. The effect of DHEA appears to be via neuronal recruitment of the steroid sensitive ACC that may be involved in pre-hippocampal memory processing. These findings are distinctive, being the first to show such beneficial effects of DHEA on memory in healthy young men.

studies.title: A randomized controlled trial of dehydroepiandrosterone in postmenopausal women with fibromyalgia.
studies.abstract: Patients with fibromyalgia (FM) consistently have adrenal hyporesponsiveness and low dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) levels. DHEA is promoted for and used by patients with FM. We tested the efficacy and safety of DHEA supplementation in ameliorating the symptoms of FM. In a double-blind crossover study, postmenopausal women with FM were randomized to DHEA supplementation (50 mg/day) or placebo for 3 months, with a one-month washout period in between. Patients were assessed monthly for well-being and pain and by medical evaluations at the beginning and the end of each treatment period. The primary outcome was well being; secondary outcomes were pain, fatigue, cognition, sexuality, functional impairment, depression, and anxiety. A total of 52 patients were randomized, 47 patients completed the DHEA treatment period, and 45 the placebo treatment period. After 3 months of treatment with 50 mg of DHEA, median DHEA sulfate blood levels had tripled, but there was no improvement in well-being, pain, fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, functional impairment, depression, or anxiety, nor in objective measurements made by physicians. Androgenic side effects (greasy skin, acne, and increased growth of body hair) were more common during the DHEA treatment period (p = 0.02). DHEA does not improve quality of life, pain, fatigue, cognitive function, mood, or functional impairment in FM.

studies.title: DHEA treatment of Alzheimer's disease: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
studies.abstract: To compare the efficacy and tolerability of dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) vs placebo in AD. Fifty-eight subjects with AD were randomized to 6 month's treatment with DHEA (50 mg per os twice a day; n = 28) or placebo (n = 30) in a multi-site, double-blind pilot trial. Primary efficacy measures assessed cognitive functioning (the AD Assessment Scale-Cognitive [ADAS-Cog]) and observer-based ratings of overall changes in severity (the Clinician's Interview-Based Impression of Change with Caregiver Input [CIBIC-Plus]). At baseline, 3 months, and 6 months, the ADAS-Cog was administered, and at 3 and 6 months, the CIBIC-Plus was administered. The 6-month time point was the primary endpoint. Nineteen DHEA-treated subjects and 14 placebo-treated subjects completed the trial. DHEA was relatively well-tolerated. DHEA treatment, relative to placebo, was not associated with improvement in ADAS-Cog scores at month 6 (last observation carried forward; p = 0.10); transient improvement was noted at month 3 (p = 0.014; cutoff for Bonferroni significance = 0.0125). No difference between treatments was seen on the CIBIC-Plus at either the 6-month or the 3-month time points. DHEA did not significantly improve cognitive performance or overall ratings of change in severity in this small-scale pilot study. A transient effect on cognitive performance may have been seen at month 3, but narrowly missed significance.

studies.title: Salivary cortisol and DHEA: association with measures of cognition and well-being in normal older men, and effects of three months of DHEA supplementation.
studies.abstract: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) is a steroid that shows a marked age-related decline in humans. Previous research suggests potential for DHEA replacement in old age to enhance cognition and well-being. We conducted a clinical trial to test these hypotheses in a non-clinical sample of 46 men aged 62-76. Participants received either 50 mg DHEA daily for 13 weeks, followed by placebo for 13 weeks, or the reverse, in a randomised double-blind cross-over trial design. Levels of salivary cortisol and DHEA were measured at 0800 h and 2000 h prior to each assessment session. Cognition was assessed with tests of speed, attention and episodic memory. Well-being was measured with questionnaires of mood and perceived health. Mood questionnaires were completed at the assessment session as well as concurrently with saliva sampling.A correlational analysis of baseline behavioural data with hormonal data, controlling for age, revealed that higher morning DHEA was associated with lower confusion (r=-0.33; P=0.04), while higher evening DHEA was associated with lower anxiety (r=-0.35; P=0.03) and lower current negative mood in the morning (r=-0.37; P=0.03). Conversely, higher morning cortisol and a morning cortisol/DHEA ratio were associated with higher anxiety (r=0.35; P=0.03), (r=0.46; P=0.004), general mood disturbance (r=0.32; P=0.046), (r=0.32; P=0.04) and higher current negative mood in the evening (r=0.37; P=0.03), (r=0.38; P=0.03). A higher morning cortisol/DHEA ratio was also associated with higher confusion (r=0.39; P=0.01) and lower visuo-spatial memory performance (r=-0.39; P=0.01). Unexpectedly, higher evening cortisol was associated with faster choice reaction time (r=-0.33; P=0.04). These findings are consistent with an impairing effect of high cortisol on episodic memory and mood in older men, which may be attenuated by DHEA. When treatment effects were analysed, no significant effects of DHEA were observed on any of the trial outcomes, providing no support for benefits of DHEA supplementation for cognition or well-being in normal older men in the shorter-term.

studies.title: DHEA replacement in women with adrenal insufficiency--pharmacokinetics, bioconversion and clinical effects on well-being, sexuality and cognition.
studies.abstract: Standard replacement for adrenal insufficiency (AI) consists of glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids while DHEA deficiency is routinely ignored. Thus, AI represents the ideal pathophysiological model of isolated DHEA deficiency. We investigated the effects of DHEA replacement in 24 women with primary and secondary AI employing a double blind, placebo-controlled, randomized crossover design. A DHEA dose of 50 mg/d was chosen based on preceding single-dose pharmacokinetics and bioconversion studies. Each patient received four months of treatment with DHEA and four months placebo, with a one-month washout period. Measurements included serum steroid hormones, somatotropic parameters and psychometric assessment of well-being, mood, cognition and sexuality. Treatment with DHEA raised the initially low serum concentrations of DHEA, DHEAS, androstenedione, and testosterone into the normal range. DHEA induced a slight increase in serum IGF-I, but only in patients with primary AI, suggesting a growth hormone-mediated effect. DHEA treatment significantly improved overall wellbeing as well as scores for depression, anxiety, and their physical correlates. Furthermore, DHEA significantly increased both sexual interest and the level of satisfaction with sex. DHEA replacement had no influence on the cognitive performance, which was already on a high level at baseline. In conclusion, DHEA replacement improves well-being and sexuality in women with adrenal insufficiency. If this is due to a direct effect of DHEA on the brain, an indirect effect via increased androgen synthesis, or both, remains to be elucidated. Long-term studies in patients of both sexes are needed to further define the role of DHEA in standard replacement for adrenal insufficiency.

studies.title: Biotransformation of oral dehydroepiandrosterone in elderly men: significant increase in circulating estrogens.
studies.abstract: The most abundant human steroids, dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and its sulfate ester DHEAS, may have a multitude of beneficial effects, but decline with age. DHEA possibly prevents immunosenescence, and as a neuroactive steroid it may influence processes of cognition and memory. Epidemiological studies revealed an inverse correlation between DHEAS levels and the incidence of cardiovascular disease in men, but not in women. To define a suitable dose for DHEA substitution in elderly men we studied pharmacokinetics and biotransformation of orally administered DHEA in 14 healthy male volunteers (mean age, 58.8 +/- 5.1 yr; mean body mass index, 25.5 +/- 1.5 kg/m2) with serum DHEAS concentrations below 4.1 micromol/L (1500 ng/mL). Diurnal blood sampling was performed on 3 occasions in a single dose, randomized, cross-over design (oral administration of placebo, 50 mg DHEA, or 100 mg DHEA). The intake of 50 mg DHEA led to an increase in serum DHEAS to mean levels of young adult men, whereas 100 mg DHEA induced supraphysiological concentrations [placebo vs. 50 mg DHEA vs. 100 mg DHEA; area under the curve (AUC) 0-12 h (mean +/- SD) for DHEA, 108 +/- 22 vs. 252 +/- 45 vs. 349 +/- 72 nmol/L x h; AUC 0-12 h for DHEAS, 33 +/- 9 vs. 114 +/- 19 vs. 164 +/- 36 micromol/L x h]. Serum testosterone and dihydrotestosterone remained unchanged after DHEA administration. In contrast, 17beta-estradiol and estrone significantly increased in a dose-dependent manner to concentrations still within the upper normal range for men [placebo vs. 50 mg DHEA vs. 100 mg DHEA; AUC 0-12 h for 17beta-estradiol, 510 +/- 198 vs. 635 +/- 156 vs. 700 +/- 209 pmol/L x h (P < 0.0001); AUC 0-12 h for estrone, 1443 +/- 269 vs. 2537 +/- 434 vs. 3254 +/- 671 pmol/L x h (P < 0.0001)]. In conclusion, 50 mg DHEA seems to be a suitable substitution dose in elderly men, as it leads to serum DHEAS concentrations usually measured in young healthy adults. The DHEA-induced increase in circulating estrogens may contribute to beneficial effects of DHEA in men.

studies.title: DHEA model of PCOS selectively alters reproductive but not metabolic or behavioral phenotypes in female Long-Evans rats.
studies.abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is the most common reproductive-metabolic disorder in women of reproductive age, yet preclinical models show considerable variability in their ability to capture its multiple diagnostic phenotypes and various non-diagnostic features. Androgen-based rodent models are widely used to mimic clinical hyperandrogenism; however, studies using dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), the most abundant circulating androgen in humans, have produced inconsistent findings across metabolic and behavioral domains. Here, we systematically evaluated a DHEA-based model of PCOS in female Long-Evans rats (N = 25), assessing reproductive, metabolic, and behavioral outcomes. To model a moderate metabolic challenge, relevant to the high comorbidity of PCOS and obesity, animals were given access to either a 10% fructose solution or water. We hypothesized that DHEA would induce PCOS-relevant phenotypes and that fructose consumption would exacerbate these effects. DHEA treatment increased ovarian testosterone levels and disrupted estrous cyclicity, consistent with key reproductive features of PCOS; however, no significant differences were observed in ovarian cyst count. In contrast, DHEA produced no robust effects across metabolic measures (including glucose tolerance, insulin resistance, and adiposity), anxiety-like behavior, or spatial working memory, and fructose exposure did not meaningfully exacerbate these outcomes. Together, these findings indicate that while DHEA reliably reproduces reproductive features of PCOS, it is insufficient to model broader metabolic and behavioral phenotypes under modest dietary challenge. These results highlight important limitations of this commonly used model and underscore the need for more robust metabolic manipulations when aiming to produce multi-system features of PCOS.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A steroid hormone your body naturally makes; sold as a supplement to raise levels that decline with age.
explanation.what_it_is: DHEA (dehydroepiandrosterone) is a steroid hormone — a molecule built from the same cholesterol backbone as testosterone and estrogen — that your adrenal glands produce throughout life. Levels peak in your 20s and 30s, then gradually drop. The supplement form (often called prasterone or DHEA) is either extracted from plant sources or synthesized in a lab, and is taken by mouth as a tablet or capsule, typically at doses of 25–200 mg per day.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Acts as a precursor to sex hormones; may boost mood and cognition through metabolites in the brain.
explanation.how_it_works: DHEA itself is not a sex hormone, but your body converts it into testosterone, estrogen, and other hormones — it is a raw material or 'precursor.' This conversion happens in many tissues, including bone, muscle, and the reproductive organs. In the brain, DHEA is also converted into compounds called neurosteroids (particularly in a pathway involving a molecule called androsterone), which may affect mood, memory, and how brain cells signal to each other. Because DHEA levels fall naturally with age, raising them could theoretically restore some of these hormone-dependent functions — but whether it does so meaningfully in humans remains an open question for many outcomes.
explanation.safety_line: Typical short-term use shows few side effects; long-term safety and effects in specific populations remain unknown.
explanation.safety_detail: Most human trials lasting weeks to several months reported DHEA to be well-tolerated with minimal adverse events — mild headache, nausea, or mood changes appeared no more often than placebo in several studies. However, the retrieved trials are generally short-term; long-term safety data (years of daily use) are sparse in the records provided. Because DHEA converts to sex hormones, populations at risk from hormone-dependent conditions (such as hormone-sensitive cancers) were typically excluded from trials.
safety_bullets: Long-term safety beyond 6–12 months is not well-studied in the retrieved records; most trials lasted weeks to a few months.
Excluded or untested: pregnant/breastfeeding women, people with hormone-sensitive cancers, severe liver or kidney disease — effects in these groups are unknown.
Potential for drug interactions with medications that rely on hormone metabolism (such as some anticonvulsants or antidepressants) has not been adequately characterized in the trials retrieved.
explanation.chem_meaning: DHEA is a lipophilic steroid — meaning it dissolves in fat and passes easily through cell membranes — thanks to its compact ring structure and modest size (288 Daltons, XLogP 3.2). This chemical property allows it to cross the blood-brain barrier and enter most tissues, which is why it can be converted to sex hormones and neurosteroids throughout the body. However, its fat-soluble nature also means it can accumulate in fatty tissues and may interact with fat-soluble vitamin absorption.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Thirteen human trials and 3 animal studies examined DHEA's effects on sexual function, particularly in women with low ovarian reserve, Sheehan syndrome (a pituitary disorder), or during menopause. A 2022 RCT in 28 women with Sheehan syndrome found DHEA improved sexual function on validated scales; a 2026 comparative trial tested DHEA against Femarelle® for menopausal sexual symptoms. A 2014 study of 208 women examined whether DHEA improved sexual outcomes during fertility treatment. Multiple small trials (n=13–38) showed improvements in sexual or reproductive measures, but findings were not uniform across all studies.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Human evidence exists but studies are inconsistent and modest in size; no pooled meta-analysis confirmed agreement across trials. The moderate grade reflects real efficacy signals in women with specific conditions (diminished ovarian reserve, Sheehan syndrome) balanced against heterogeneity and lack of large confirmatory trials.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Ten human trials and 9 animal studies were retrieved, with a pooled odds ratio of 2.22 (95% CI 1.05–4.71) favoring DHEA for improving ovarian response in poor responders undergoing IVF. Key studies include a 2013 meta-analysis and a 2023 systematic review of 2,323 participants comparing DHEA, CoQ10, and other supplements for poor ovarian response. An RCT of 208 women (2014) and one of 38 women (2013) showed DHEA supplementation improved spontaneous pregnancy rates in women with diminished ovarian reserve. A 2004 trial of 14 women with Sjögren's syndrome also examined fertility markers.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: The pooled odds ratio shows a meaningful effect, but precision is modest (~2,677 participants verified across 8 studies; true total likely larger but many abstracts omit sample size). Only 6 primary human RCTs and 2 pooled analyses were retrieved — below the threshold for the highest tier. The effect is real but rests on limited independent replications.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Four human trials and 1 animal study examined DHEA's effect on muscle strength. A 2010 RCT found DHEA combined with exercise improved muscle strength and physical function in frail older women. The 2007 DAWN study (n=115) tested DHEA in older adults and measured physical function. A 2008 trial examined DHEA in myotonic dystrophy type 1 (a genetic muscle disease). A 2006 trial tested DHEA in elderly men and women. A 2024 animal study in 24 ovariectomized rats showed DHEA enhanced fracture healing, suggesting effects on bone and possibly muscle quality.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Sample size is modest (~139 participants verified across 2 of 5 studies), making the effect estimate imprecise and potentially unstable. Human evidence exists in older and special populations (frail elderly, muscle disorders), but the field lacks large, independent confirmatory trials to firmly establish efficacy.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Eleven human trials and 1 animal study examined DHEA's effects on cognition, mood, and memory. A 2020 systematic review focused on DHEA in Alzheimer's disease and cognitive decline. A 2010 RCT of 44 people tested pregnenolone and DHEA as add-ons to antipsychotics in schizophrenia. A 2008 RCT of 106 people with primary adrenal insufficiency (a condition requiring DHEA replacement) measured cognition during long-term DHEA therapy. A 2006 RCT tested DHEA in postmenopausal women; another 2006 trial in healthy young men examined effects on episodic memory, cortisol, and mood. Most studies found improvements in specific cognitive domains or mood, but results were not consistent across all measures or populations.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Human evidence is present (11 trials), but only a single meta-analysis or systematic review exists in the retrieved records, and its conclusions have not been independently verified by other pooled analyses. This limits confidence; moderate grade reflects real signals without high-certainty replication.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base is predominantly human (28 human trials and meta-analyses) with supplemental animal studies (14 animal trials). Most human trials are small to modest-sized RCTs (n=13–208), many conducted 2004–2020, with a few more recent studies (2022–2026). Human studies focus on specific populations: women with diminished ovarian reserve or Sheehan syndrome, frail elderly, people with Alzheimer's disease or schizophrenia, and those with adrenal insufficiency. Animal studies include rodent models of osteoporosis and muscle aging. The predominance of human data and real-world populations (not just healthy volunteers) provides reasonable confidence, but most outcomes lack the large, multi-center trials needed for high-certainty grading.
explanation.open_questions: The records provided do not include adequately large trials in healthy, younger adults — most cognition and muscle studies involve older or diseased populations. No studies retrieved examined very long-term use (>1 year) systematically. For fertility and sexual function, the reasons for inconsistency across studies (dose, duration, baseline DHEA levels, specific populations) are not fully explored in the abstracts. Whether DHEA's benefits apply equally to men and women, and whether responses depend on baseline DHEA deficiency, remain unclear from the retrieved records. These gaps are visible in the sample provided; the full literature may address some of them.

appraisal.headline: Across all four outcomes, no pooled meta-analytic evidence confirms consistency of effect; most individual trials are small (median n=25–46), and heterogeneous populations (Sheehan syndrome, fibromyalgia, Alzheimer's, poor ovarian reserve, elderly frail) limit generalizability of any single finding.

concerns.issue: No extractable pooled effect for 3 of 4 outcomes
concerns.detail: Sexual function, muscle strength, and cognition are each graded Moderate despite the engine noting 'no pooled analysis confirms they agree' (sexual function), 'no pooled effect extractable' (muscle strength), and 'single meta-analysis not independently replicated' (cognition). This means the grade rests on narrative consistency rather than a quantitative synthesis, making it impossible to assess whether the signal is real or scattered noise across heterogeneous small trials.

concerns.issue: Fertility outcome inflated by one very large observational study
concerns.detail: The fertility/ovarian function pooled OR of 2.22 [1.05–4.71] is nominally significant but rests on a 2323-participant systematic review (2023) alongside RCTs of n=14–208. The meta-analysis and systematic review are summary-level evidence; if they heavily weight one large observational cohort, the confidence interval is artificially narrow. The records do not specify internal study weights, so a single large uncontrolled study may be driving the point estimate while smaller RCTs diverge.

concerns.issue: Extreme incompleteness in sample size reporting
concerns.detail: For sexual function, only 8 of 16 studies report n; for fertility, only 8 of 19; for muscle strength, only 2 of 5. This means the median and summary statistics are biased upward (small studies that failed to report n are unknown), and the true precision of any pooled estimate is worse than stated. One small unpublished or omitted negative trial could shift a borderline result.

The sexual function and cognition cohorts mix postmenopausal women (2011, 2006), Sheehan syndrome (2022, a rare pituitary disorder), schizophrenia adjunctive therapy (2010), Alzheimer's disease (2003, 2020), elderly frail (2008, 2007), and fibromyalgia (2005). No subgroup analysis by pathophysiology is visible in the records. An effect seen in adrenal insufficiency patients (where DHEA is physiologically deficient) may not generalize to postmenopausal women with normal DHEA levels.

concerns.issue: Muscle strength evidence threshold nearly unmet
concerns.detail: Only 5 total studies for muscle strength (4 RCT, 1 animal) with verified n in only 2 studies (n=24 and n=115); median reported is 115 but that is driven by a single large study. The engine itself notes 'imprecision: modest verified sample (~139 participants)' — this is below standard thresholds for a robust evidence grade. A single strong outlier trial dominates the apparent signal.

appraisal.mechanism_check: DHEA is proposed to work via conversion to androgens and neurosteroids (androsterone mentioned in a 2015 RCT title). For fertility/ovarian function, a mitochondrial biogenesis pathway is mentioned (2021 clinical trial). These are plausible mechanisms, but the clinical claims (sexual function, pregnancy rates, cognition) are downstream endpoints; the gap between 'DHEA increases mitochondrial ATP' and 'women conceive more often' is substantial and requires multiple intermediate steps (ovarian reserve, oocyte quality, embryo competence) that are not directly measured in most trials. For cognition, the mechanism (cortisol modulation, neuroprotection) is even more indirect and not validated by the retrieved evidence.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that (1) three outcomes lack any pooled quantitative synthesis — they rest on voting rules across tiny, diverse trials, a method prone to publication bias; (2) the one outcome with a pooled OR (fertility, 2.22) is driven by observational and summary-level evidence with opaque weighting, and its CI includes 1.05, meaning the lower bound is barely above noise; (3) across all four outcomes, sample sizes are small (median ≤46), populations are clinically heterogeneous, and selective reporting of n is visible — these are hallmarks of a literature vulnerable to bias. The Moderate grade may reflect 'some signal in some populations' rather than 'DHEA reliably improves these outcomes.'
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: A pre-registered, adequately powered RCT (n≥200) in a single, well-defined population (e.g., women with diminished ovarian reserve undergoing IVF, or postmenopausal women with sexual dysfunction) with rigorous outcome assessment and a published protocol would resolve whether the effect is real or inflated by bias. Alternatively, a meta-analysis with explicit risk-of-bias assessment and sensitivity analysis removing non-RCT evidence would clarify whether the fertility OR is robust to study design.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Una hormona esteroide que tu cuerpo produce naturalmente; se vende como suplemento para elevar los niveles que disminuyen con la edad.
explanation_es.what_it_is: DHEA (dehidroepiandrosterona) es una hormona esteroide — una molécula construida a partir del mismo esqueleto de colesterol que la testosterona y el estrógeno — que tus glándulas suprarrenales producen a lo largo de la vida. Los niveles alcanzan su pico en los 20s y 30s, y luego disminuyen gradualmente. La forma de suplemento (a menudo llamada prasterona o DHEA) se extrae de fuentes vegetales o se sintetiza en un laboratorio, y se toma por vía oral como tableta o cápsula, típicamente en dosis de 25–200 mg por día.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Actúa como precursor de hormonas sexuales; puede potenciar el estado de ánimo y la cognición a través de metabolitos en el cerebro.
explanation_es.how_it_works: La DHEA en sí no es una hormona sexual, pero tu cuerpo la convierte en testosterona, estrógeno y otras hormonas — es una materia prima o 'precursor'. Esta conversión ocurre en muchos tejidos, incluyendo hueso, músculo y órganos reproductivos. En el cerebro, la DHEA también se convierte en compuestos llamados neuroesteroides (particularmente en una vía que involucra una molécula llamada androstenona), que pueden afectar el estado de ánimo, la memoria y cómo las células cerebrales se comunican entre sí. Debido a que los niveles de DHEA disminuyen naturalmente con la edad, elevarlos podría teóricamente restaurar algunas de estas funciones dependientes de hormonas — pero si lo hace de manera significativa en humanos sigue siendo una pregunta abierta para muchos resultados.
explanation_es.safety_line: El uso típico a corto plazo muestra pocos efectos secundarios; la seguridad a largo plazo y los efectos en poblaciones específicas permanecen desconocidos.
explanation_es.safety_detail: La mayoría de los ensayos humanos que duraron semanas a varios meses reportaron que la DHEA fue bien tolerada con eventos adversos mínimos — dolor de cabeza leve, náuseas o cambios de humor aparecieron no más frecuentemente que el placebo en varios estudios. Sin embargo, los ensayos recuperados son generalmente a corto plazo; los datos de seguridad a largo plazo (años de uso diario) son escasos en los registros proporcionados. Debido a que la DHEA se convierte en hormonas sexuales, las poblaciones en riesgo de condiciones dependientes de hormonas (como cánceres sensibles a hormonas) fueron típicamente excluidas de los ensayos.
safety_bullets: La seguridad a largo plazo más allá de 6–12 meses no está bien estudiada en los registros recuperados; la mayoría de los ensayos duraron semanas a algunos meses.
Excluidas o no probadas: mujeres embarazadas/lactantes, personas con cánceres sensibles a hormonas, enfermedad hepática o renal grave — los efectos en estos grupos son desconocidos.

El potencial de interacciones farmacológicas con medicamentos que dependen del metabolismo de hormonas (como algunos anticonvulsivos o antidepresivos) no ha sido adecuadamente caracterizado en los ensayos recuperados.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: La DHEA es un esteroide lipofílico — lo que significa que se disuelve en grasas y pasa fácilmente a través de membranas celulares — gracias a su estructura de anillos compacta y su tamaño modesto (288 Daltons, XLogP 3.2). Esta propiedad química le permite cruzar la barrera hematoencefálica e ingresar a la mayoría de los tejidos, lo cual es por qué puede convertirse en hormonas sexuales y neuroesteroides en todo el cuerpo. Sin embargo, su naturaleza soluble en grasas también significa que puede acumularse en tejidos adiposos e interactuar con la absorción de vitaminas liposolubles.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Trece ensayos humanos y 3 estudios en animales examinaron los efectos de la DHEA en la función sexual, particularmente en mujeres con baja reserva ovárica, síndrome de Sheehan (un trastorno hipofisario), o durante la menopausia. Un ECA de 2022 en 28 mujeres con síndrome de Sheehan encontró que la DHEA mejoró la función sexual en escalas validadas; un ensayo comparativo de 2026 probó DHEA contra Femarelle® para síntomas sexuales menopáusicos. Un estudio de 2014 de 208 mujeres examinó si la DHEA mejoraba los resultados sexuales durante el tratamiento de fertilidad. Múltiples ensayos pequeños (n=13–38) mostraron mejoras en medidas sexuales o reproductivas, pero los hallazgos no fueron uniformes en todos los estudios.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La evidencia humana existe pero los estudios son inconsistentes y modestos en tamaño; ningún metanálisis agrupado confirmó acuerdo entre ensayos. La calificación moderada refleja señales de eficacia reales en mujeres con condiciones específicas (reserva ovárica disminuida, síndrome de Sheehan) equilibradas contra heterogeneidad y falta de grandes ensayos confirmatorios.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Diez ensayos humanos y 9 estudios en animales fueron recuperados, con una razón de probabilidades agrupada de 2.22 (95% CI 1.05–4.71) a favor de la DHEA para mejorar la respuesta ovárica en pobres respondedoras sometidas a FIV. Los estudios clave incluyen un metanálisis de 2013 y una revisión sistemática de 2023 de 2,323 participantes comparando DHEA, CoQ10 y otros suplementos para baja respuesta ovárica. Un ECA de 208 mujeres (2014) y uno de 38 mujeres (2013) mostraron que la suplementación con DHEA mejoró las tasas de embarazo espontáneo en mujeres con reserva ovárica disminuida. Un ensayo de 2004 de 14 mujeres con síndrome de Sjögren también examinó marcadores de fertilidad.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La razón de probabilidades agrupada muestra un efecto significativo, pero la precisión es modesta (~2,677 participantes verificados en 8 estudios; el total verdadero probablemente mayor pero muchos resúmenes omiten el tamaño de muestra). Solo 6 ECA primarios humanos y 2 análisis agrupados fueron recuperados — por debajo del umbral para el nivel más alto. El efecto es real pero se basa en replicaciones independientes limitadas.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cuatro ensayos humanos y 1 estudio en animales examinaron el efecto de la DHEA en la fuerza muscular. Un ECA de 2010 encontró que la DHEA combinada con ejercicio mejoró la fuerza muscular y la función física en mujeres mayores frágiles. El estudio DAWN de 2007 (n=115) probó DHEA en adultos mayores y midió la función física. Un ensayo de 2008 examinó la DHEA en distrofia miotónica tipo 1 (una enfermedad muscular genética). Un ensayo de 2006 probó la DHEA en hombres y mujeres de edad avanzada. Un estudio en animales de 2024 en 24 ratas ovariectomizadas mostró que la DHEA mejoró la cicatrización ósea, sugiriendo efectos en la calidad ósea y posiblemente muscular.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: El tamaño de muestra es modesto (~139 participantes verificados en 2 de 5 estudios), lo que hace que la estimación del efecto sea imprecisa y potencialmente inestable. La evidencia humana existe en poblaciones especiales y mayores (ancianos frágiles, trastornos musculares), pero el campo carece de grandes ensayos confirmatorios independientes para establecer firmemente la eficacia.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Once ensayos humanos y 1 estudio en animales examinaron los efectos de la DHEA en la cognición, el estado de ánimo y la memoria. Una revisión sistemática de 2020 se enfocó en la DHEA en la enfermedad de Alzheimer y el declive cognitivo. Un ECA de 2010 de 44 personas probó pregnenolona y DHEA como adiciones a antipsicóticos en esquizofrenia. Un ECA de 2008 de 106 personas con insuficiencia suprarrenal primaria (una condición que requiere reemplazo de DHEA) midió la cognición durante la terapia a largo plazo con DHEA. Un ECA de 2006 probó DHEA en mujeres posmenopáusicas; otro ensayo de 2006 en hombres jóvenes sanos examinó efectos en la memoria episódica, cortisol y estado de ánimo. La mayoría de los estudios encontraron mejoras en dominios cognitivos específicos o estado de ánimo, pero los resultados no fueron consistentes en todas las medidas o poblaciones.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La evidencia humana está presente (11 ensayos), pero solo existe un único metanálisis o revisión sistemática en los registros recuperados, y sus conclusiones no han sido verificadas independientemente por otros análisis agrupados. Esto limita la confianza; la calificación moderada refleja señales reales sin replicación de alta certeza.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia es predominantemente humana (28 ensayos humanos y metanálisis) con estudios en animales complementarios (14 ensayos en animales). La mayoría de los ensayos humanos son ECA de tamaño pequeño a modesto (n=13–208), muchos conducidos 2004–2020, con algunos estudios más recientes (2022–2026). Los estudios humanos se enfocan en poblaciones específicas: mujeres con reserva ovárica disminuida o síndrome de Sheehan, ancianos frágiles, personas con enfermedad de Alzheimer o esquizofrenia, y aquellos con insuficiencia suprarrenal. Los estudios en animales incluyen modelos roedores de osteoporosis y envejecimiento muscular. El predominio de datos humanos y poblaciones del mundo real (no solo voluntarios sanos) proporciona confianza razonable, pero la mayoría de los resultados carecen de los grandes ensayos multicéntricos necesarios para calificaciones de alta certeza.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados no incluyen ensayos adecuadamente grandes en adultos sanos y más jóvenes — la mayoría de los estudios de cognición y músculos involucran poblaciones mayores o enfermas. Ningún estudio recuperado examinó sistemáticamente el uso a muy largo plazo (>1 año). Para fertilidad y función sexual, las razones de la inconsistencia entre estudios (dosis, duración, niveles basales de DHEA, poblaciones específicas) no se exploran completamente en los resúmenes. Si los beneficios de la DHEA se aplican igualmente a hombres y mujeres, y si las respuestas dependen del déficit basal de DHEA, permanecen sin claridad en los registros recuperados. Estas brechas son visibles en la muestra proporcionada; la literatura completa puede abordar algunas de ellas.

appraisal_es.headline: En los cuatro resultados, ninguna evidencia metanalítica agrupada confirma consistencia del efecto; la mayoría de ensayos individuales son pequeños (n mediana=25–46), y las poblaciones heterogéneas (síndrome de Sheehan, fibromialgia, Alzheimer, baja reserva ovárica, ancianos frágiles) limitan la generalización de cualquier hallazgo único.

concerns.issue: Sin efecto agrupado extractable para 3 de 4 resultados
concerns.detail: La función sexual, la fuerza muscular y la cognición están cada una calificadas como Moderada a pesar de que el motor nota 'ningún análisis agrupado confirma que coincidan' (función sexual), 'ningún efecto agrupado extractable' (fuerza muscular) y 'único metanálisis no replicado independientemente' (cognición). Esto significa que la calificación descansa en consistencia narrativa en lugar de síntesis cuantitativa, lo que hace imposible evaluar si la señal es real o ruido disperso en ensayos pequeños heterogéneos.

concerns.issue: Resultado de fertilidad inflado por un estudio observacional muy grande
concerns.detail: La OR agrupada de fertilidad/función ovárica de 2.22 [1.05–4.71] es nominalmente significativa pero descansa en una revisión sistemática de 2323 participantes (2023) junto con ECA de n=14–208. El metanálisis y la revisión sistemática son evidencia a nivel de resumen; si ponderan fuertemente una cohorte observacional grande única, el intervalo de confianza es artificialmente estrecho. Los registros no especifican pesos internos de estudios, por lo que un único estudio observacional grande no controlado puede estar impulsando la estimación puntual mientras que los ECA más pequeños divergen.

concerns.issue: Incompletitud extrema en el reporte del tamaño de muestra
concerns.detail: Para función sexual, solo 8 de 16 estudios reportan n; para fertilidad, solo 8 de 19; para fuerza muscular, solo 2 de 5. Esto significa que la mediana y estadísticas de resumen están sesgadas hacia arriba (estudios pequeños que no reportaron n son desconocidos), y la verdadera precisión de cualquier estimación agrupada es peor que la indicada. Un único ensayo pequeño no publicado u omitido negativo podría cambiar un resultado borderline.

Las cohortes de función sexual y cognición mezclan mujeres posmenopáusicas (2011, 2006), síndrome de Sheehan (2022, un trastorno hipofisario raro), terapia adyuvante de esquizofrenia (2010), enfermedad de Alzheimer (2003, 2020), ancianos frágiles (2008, 2007) y fibromialgia (2005). Ningún análisis de subgrupos por fisiopatología es visible en los registros. Un efecto observado en pacientes con insuficiencia adrenal (donde DHEA es fisiológicamente deficiente) puede no generalizarse a mujeres posmenopáusicas con niveles normales de DHEA.

concerns.issue: Umbral de evidencia de fuerza muscular casi no alcanzado
concerns.detail: Solo 5 estudios totales para fuerza muscular (4 ECA, 1 animal) con n verificado en solo 2 estudios (n=24 y n=115); la mediana reportada es 115 pero está impulsada por un único estudio grande. El motor mismo nota 'imprecisión: muestra verificada modesta (~139 participantes)' — esto está por debajo de umbrales estándar para una calificación de evidencia robusta. Un único ensayo atípico fuerte domina la señal aparente.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: Se propone que DHEA actúe mediante conversión a andrógenos y neuroesteroides (androstenona mencionada en un título de ECA de 2015). Para fertilidad/función ovárica, se menciona una vía de biogénesis mitocondrial (ensayo clínico de 2021). Estos son mecanismos plausibles, pero los reclamos clínicos (función sexual, tasas de embarazo, cognición) son puntos finales aguas abajo; la brecha entre 'DHEA aumenta ATP mitocondrial' y 'las mujeres conciben más frecuentemente' es sustancial y requiere múltiples pasos intermedios (reserva ovárica, calidad de oocito, competencia embrionaria) que no se miden directamente en la mayoría de ensayos. Para cognición, el mecanismo (modulación de cortisol, neuroprotección) es aún más indirecto y no validado por la evidencia recuperada.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico notaría que (1) tres resultados carecen de cualquier síntesis cuantitativa agrupada — descansan en reglas de votación entre ensayos minúsculos y diversos, un método propenso a sesgo de publicación; (2) el único resultado con una OR agrupada (fertilidad, 2.22) es impulsado por evidencia observacional y a nivel de resumen con ponderación opaca, y su IC incluye 1.05, lo que significa que el límite inferior apenas está por encima del ruido; (3) en los cuatro resultados, los tamaños de muestra son pequeños (mediana ≤46), las poblaciones son clínicamente heterogéneas, y el reporte selectivo de n es visible — estas son características de una literatura vulnerable al sesgo. La calificación Moderada puede reflejar 'algo de señal en algunas poblaciones' en lugar de 'DHEA mejora confiablemente estos resultados'.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un ECA preespecificado, adecuadamente potenciado (n≥200) en una población única bien definida (p. ej., mujeres con baja reserva ovárica sometidas a FIV, o mujeres posmenopáusicas con disfunción sexual) con evaluación rigurosa de resultados y protocolo publicado resolvería si el efecto es real o inflado por sesgo. Alternativamente, un metanálisis con evaluación explícita de riesgo de sesgo y análisis de sensibilidad eliminando evidencia no-ECA aclararía si la OR de fertilidad es robusta al diseño del estudio.
